response.title: what size portable power station do i need to run a refrigerator
response.answer:
For a typical household refrigerator, I recommend a portable power station with 1,000–2,000 Wh of battery capacity and at least a 1,500 W pure sine wave inverter.

The exact size depends on your refrigerator and how long you want it to run.

Recommended power station size

Battery capacity

	

Estimated refrigerator runtime




500 Wh

	

4–8 hours




1,000 Wh

	

8–16 hours




1,500 Wh

	

12–24 hours




2,000 Wh

	

16–32 hours




3,000 Wh

	

24–48 hours




4,000 Wh

	

32–64 hours

Estimates assume a refrigerator averaging 50–100 W over time, with approximately 85% usable energy after inverter losses. Actual runtime varies.
Two specifications that matter

1. Battery capacity (Wh): How long it runs

A refrigerator typically consumes around 1–2 kWh per day, although efficient modern models may use considerably less.

For example, if your refrigerator consumes 1.2 kWh daily:

1,000 Wh battery → approximately 17 hours

2,000 Wh battery → approximately 34 hours

3,000 Wh battery → approximately 51 hours

2. Inverter output (W): Whether it can start the refrigerator

A refrigerator's compressor draws a brief surge of electricity when starting.

Typical requirements:

Running power: 100–250 W while the compressor is operating

Startup surge: approximately 600–1,500 W, sometimes higher

Recommended inverter: 1,500–2,000 W continuous output with adequate surge capacity

A large battery with an undersized inverter might not start your refrigerator.

For a typical household refrigerator, I recommend a **portable power station with 1,000–2,000 Wh of battery capacity and at least a 1,500 W pure sine wave inverter**.

The exact size depends on your refrigerator and how long you want it to run.

## Recommended power station size

| Battery capacity | Estimated refrigerator runtime |
|---|---|
| 500 Wh | 4–8 hours |
| 1,000 Wh | 8–16 hours |
| 1,500 Wh | 12–24 hours |
| 2,000 Wh | 16–32 hours |
| 3,000 Wh | 24–48 hours |
| 4,000 Wh | 32–64 hours |

<caption>Estimates assume a refrigerator averaging 50–100 W over time, with approximately 85% usable energy after inverter losses. Actual runtime varies.</caption>

## Two specifications that matter

**1. Battery capacity (Wh): How long it runs**

A refrigerator typically consumes around 1–2 kWh per day, although efficient modern models may use considerably less.

For example, if your refrigerator consumes 1.2 kWh daily:

- 1,000 Wh battery → approximately 17 hours
- 2,000 Wh battery → approximately 34 hours
- 3,000 Wh battery → approximately 51 hours

**2. Inverter output (W): Whether it can start the refrigerator**

A refrigerator's compressor draws a brief surge of electricity when starting.

Typical requirements:

- Running power: 100–250 W while the compressor is operating
- Startup surge: approximately 600–1,500 W, sometimes higher
- Recommended inverter: 1,500–2,000 W continuous output with adequate surge capacity

A large battery with an undersized inverter might not start your refrigerator.

## Help me size it accurately

{@body const [model,setModel] = DIL.useState("")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Size a portable power station for my "+({full:"full-size refrigerator",mini:"mini fridge",side:"side-by-side refrigerator",garage:"older garage refrigerator"}[fridge])+" for "+duration+" hours. Refrigerator model or energy usage: "+(model||"unknown")+". Recommend battery Wh and inverter W.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What kind of refrigerator?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={fridge} onChange={setFridge}>
        <radio value="full">Standard full-size refrigerator</radio>
        <radio value="side">Large side-by-side refrigerator</radio>
        <radio value="mini">Mini fridge</radio>
        <radio value="garage">Older garage refrigerator</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>How long do you want it to run?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={duration} onChange={setDuration}>
        <radio value="8">8 hours</radio>
        <radio value="12">12 hours</radio>
        <radio value="24">24 hours</radio>
        <radio value="48">48 hours</radio>
        <radio value="72">72 hours</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Refrigerator model or energy usage (optional)</label>
      <input placeholder="e.g. 500 kWh/year or model number" value={model} onChange={setModel}/>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate recommended power station size <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>
